related_questions.question: Can you stop an eviction by paying NC?

text_blocks.snippet: In North Carolina, if an eviction is solely due to non-payment of rent, the tenant can potentially stop the eviction by paying the full amount of rent owed, including any court costs, at the eviction hearing. This payment must be in cash, money order, or certified check, and a receipt clearly stating "Paid in Full" is crucial.
snippet_highlighted_words: if an eviction is solely due to non-payment of rent, the tenant can potentially stop the eviction by paying the full amount of rent owed, including any court costs, at the eviction hearing

list.title: "Redemption" or "Cure":
list.snippet: In North Carolina, this process of paying to stop an eviction is sometimes referred to as "redemption" or "curing" the default.

list.title: Court Costs:
list.snippet: Along with the unpaid rent, the tenant must also pay any court costs associated with the eviction case.

list.title: Receipt:
list.snippet: A written and dated receipt from the landlord, specifying that the payment is for the full amount owed, is essential to stop the eviction.

list.title: Not all Evictions can be Stopped:
list.snippet: If the eviction is based on reasons other than non-payment of rent, like lease violations (e.g., having a pet when prohibited), paying rent will likely not stop the eviction.

list.title: Appeal:
list.snippet: Even if the eviction is dismissed due to payment, the tenant can still appeal the decision to district court within 10 days, and continuing to pay rent on time while the appeal is pending may allow them to remain in the property until the appeal is resolved.
